column3: Distinguishes رسول الله and كلمة الله while joining faith in Allah and His messengers under sole ownership.
The immediate calf episode contrasts a powerless object that neither speaks nor guides with the guiding messenger.
Directly pairs Allah's acts of causing death and life.
Addresses الناس with a messenger, faith, and Allah's ownership of heaven and earth.
Immediate repentance context adds little beyond the need to return after going astray.
Links a guidance sent to all with following it and its protective outcome.
Addresses الناس and grounds exclusive divinity in Allah's creative provision from heaven and earth.
The immediate leadership dispute supplies only a distant contextual contrast.
Presents life, death, and renewed life as one ordered divine sequence.
Reiterates faith in Allah, His messenger, and what is sent down.
Immediate prayer for forgiveness does not materially clarify the address or commission.
A prophetic refusal of rival worship and desires frames guided following as non-autonomous.
Directly joins exclusive divinity with giving life and causing death.
The calf warning reinforces rejection of association but adds little after the prior immediate cards.
Tests a human claim about life and death against Allah's cosmic ordering, marking a boundary for delegated power.
Directly combines heaven-and-earth ownership with giving life and death and denies alternative protection.
Immediate repentance and faith add only a general response pattern.
Its imperative to follow those who are guided clarifies following as responsive to guidance, not ownership of it.
Compact parallel of Allah's ownership of heaven and earth, life, death, and power.
The immediate tablet context pairs guidance and mercy with reverent reception before the messenger is named.
Cosmic gathering has no clear route to the verse's messenger, faith, or life-death claim.
The messenger disclaims treasury and unseen knowledge and follows only what is revealed.
Immediate Mosaic context keeps guidance, error, and divine protection in view but does not specify the 7:158 commission.
Connects Allah's كلمة with His sent servants, supporting the relation between divine words and messengership.
The designation النبي and his belief in Allah parallel the messenger's own believing stance.
The immediately preceding covenant context names faith in Allah's signs and leads directly into the 7:157-158 messenger description.
A gathering of all people is only a remote parallel to the universal address.
Places all intercession and heaven-earth ownership with Allah, supporting exclusive authority without the messenger element.
The directly preceding card identifies the same النبي الأمي and joins belief, support, and following the sent light.
Heaven-earth sovereignty and the powerlessness of invoked rivals support the exclusive-authority clause.
Faith in Allah and His messengers follows divine selection among messengers, but the setting is less direct.
The nearby creation account and channel links do not yield a specific contribution to 7:158.
Heaven-earth ownership and Allah's active judgment reinforce divine sovereignty.
Links this prophet, believers, and following Abraham, adding continuity rather than the universal commission itself.
The nearby rejection of association supports exclusivity only in general terms.
Directly contrasts following what is sent down from the Lord with following other protectors.
Reiterates Allah as giver of life and death, though this core claim is already repeatedly established.
Follower-community language is too indirect to explain the commanded following in 7:158.
Presents a messenger as confirming prior scripture and announcing a later messenger, clarifying a connected messenger sequence.
A sent messenger's open warning to his people gives a localized parallel to public proclamation.
Allah's complete command and possible guidance of all people are too indirect for the focus relation.
The contrast link marks a boundary around a false utterance, not positive support for Allah's كلمات.
Physical roads and orientation provide only an indirect image of guidance.
Places the messenger's worship, life, and death wholly for Allah, extending the self-believing stance of 7:158.
Divine power over the Messiah, his mother, and all on earth marks a boundary against elevating a created figure.
Relates refusal of Allah's signs to lack of guidance, clarifying the response side of faith and guidance.
Calls for collective attachment to Allah and non-division so that guidance is received communally.
Its life-from-dead-earth pattern supports life-giving only; the contrast link limits further use of its reading.
Scripture and furqan are given to Moses for guidance, supplying a prior revelation-guidance parallel.
Frames the messengers' delivery of their Lord's messages as an accountable, completed conveyance.
Prepared earthly paths offer only a physical analogy for being guided.
Contrasts following what Allah sent down with inherited paths that lack guidance.
Faith in Allah and His messenger is present but adds no distinct relation after closer parallels.
Preserved contrary case: inherited tracks are called guidance without their destination being tested.
Exclusive divinity, enduring life, and heaven-earth possession reinforce the sovereignty frame.
Universal gathering is a distant and redundant parallel to the address to all people.
Shows that recognizing a messenger need not produce following, and refusal is linked to loss of guidance.
Explicitly sets Allah's guidance over socially demanded following of other paths.
Places Allah and His messenger above competing loyalties and links refusal with lack of guidance.
Provides a contrary pattern: following a rebellious authority amid argument without knowledge.
Shared faith in Allah and what was sent down supplies a broad cross-scriptural parallel only.
Directly asks about power to give life to the dead, reinforcing the life-death clause.
Its faith and guidance language is embedded in a separate giving example and adds little.
The bare pairing of living and dead lacks a usable link to the focus claim.
Regulates conduct toward the messenger but does not clarify his universal commission or following.
The objection to coming forth alive after death supplies a direct life-and-death boundary case.
A shared direction can analogize collective orientation, but it is not the commanded following of 7:158.
Affirms that none can misdirect one whom Allah guides, without adding the messenger relation.
Its refuge from arrogance and judgment denial has no specific route to the focus.
Links undiluted faith with security and being guided, clarifying an outcome of faithful response.
Mention of Allah and His messenger witnessing deeds is not a material parallel to the commission.
Contrasts following conjecture with truth, preserving a contrary standard for what may be followed.
A repudiated word and opposition to Allah and His messenger offer only a peripheral contrast.
Even universal disbelief does not affect Allah's independence, a limited parallel to the address of all people.
Its social-meal regulations do not clarify the focus despite the auxiliary channel route.
Directly states Allah gives life, causes death, and remains the inheritor, adding final possession.
The prophet's ethical pledge procedure is a localized obedience setting, not the focus's commission.
Allah establishes truth through His كلمات, supporting the verse's reference to His words.
كلمات and leadership after testing offer a distant, qualified parallel with no direct messenger relation.
Contrasts a revealed Arabic judgment with following desires after knowledge has come.
Brief faith and temporary enjoyment do not specify a relevant focus relation.
The isolated phrase about following a means is too underspecified to explain following the messenger.
Its exclusive-divinity confession within a repentance narrative supports only one limited clause.
The sending of birds is not informative about the divine messenger or guidance claims.
Human unity and a prior divine كلمة frame delayed judgment, but only remotely touch the universal address.
Expands the life-death claim through transformations between living, dead, and revived earth.
Explicitly joins faith in Allah, His messenger, and revealed books, though it is broader than 7:158.
Preserves the contrary case of following Iblis rather than remaining with believers.
A messenger recites clarifying Allah-signs to move believers from darkness to light.
The messenger is not unprecedented, follows only revelation, and is only a clear warner.
The speaker is guided by his Lord to a straight way, directly paralleling the goal of following for guidance.
Shared mortality of the messenger and others supports only the death clause, already well covered.
Exclusive divinity is illustrated through the availability of night, a distant support for the sovereignty claim.
Directly connects obeying Allah and the messenger with guidance while limiting the messenger to clear delivery.
A detailed death-and-revival sign reinforces divine power to restore life.
Attributes guidance to Allah, clarifying the source behind the guided result of following.
Debt documentation has no material relation to the focus.
A true revelation from the Lord authorizes a messenger's warning so that a people may be guided.
Inheritance allocation does not clarify the focus.
The collective drowning account does not add to the messenger, guidance, or life-death relation.
A prayer for a messenger among the community joins recitation, teaching, and purification.
Faith is extended across Allah, revelation, and the messenger line without separating among them.
Believers affirm Allah, angels, books, and messengers while refusing to split the messenger line.
The address includes أهل الكتاب and الأميين and limits the messenger to conveyance after submission is presented.
Allah's covenant with prophets frames later messenger confirmation as a shared prophetic obligation.
Faith in Allah, what was sent down, and the prophets supplies a broad parallel to believing Allah and His كلمات.
A messenger among believers recites signs and teaches, clarifying an enacted messenger role.
Directly orders obedience to Allah and the messenger and returns disputes to both authorities.
Makes obedience to the messenger inseparable from obedience to Allah.
Preserves the contrary attempt to believe in Allah while differentiating among His messengers.
Affirms those who believe in Allah and all His messengers without differentiation.
A messenger comes to clarify matters previously concealed, joining public arrival and divine disclosure.
Allah guides through what follows His approval from darkness toward peace and straight paths.
A messenger comes after an interval so that no claim of missing bearer of good news or warning remains.
The messenger is charged to convey what was sent down from his Lord.
Revelation is a warning for the addressees and whomever it reaches, with exclusive divinity stated in the same declaration.
Combines exclusive divinity, creation of all things, and worship of Allah.
Directly commands following what has been revealed from the Lord and rejects rival deities.
Identifies a straight path to be followed and contrasts it with dispersing paths.
A blessed book is sent down to be followed so that mercy may be received.
A detailed book arrives upon knowledge as guidance and mercy for believers.
Directly has the messenger follow only what is revealed from his Lord, calling it insight, guidance, and mercy.
Allah sends His messenger with guidance and the religion of truth for public manifestation.
Explicitly asks whether the one who guides to truth is more entitled to be followed.
Directly attributes life and death to Allah and return to Him.
What comes from the Lord is described through healing, guidance, and mercy for believers.
Truth has come from the Lord and guidance or error is located in each response.
The message is called a reminder for all worlds without a requested reward.
The messenger declares a path of calling to Allah upon insight and distinguishes himself from associators.
A sent-down book brings people from darkness to light by their Lord's permission.
Each messenger is sent in his people's language, while guidance and error remain under Allah's will.
It is a proclamation for الناس, warning through it and asserting one God.
The sending of revelation to chosen servants carries the exclusive-divinity warning.
Every community receives a messenger centered on worship of Allah and avoidance of false authorities.
The messenger receives the reminder to clarify what has been sent down to people.
A book is sent down as clarification, guidance, mercy, and good news for submitters.
The Qur'an guides to what is most upright and announces believers' outcome.
The Qur'an is sent with truth, and the messenger is sent as bearer of good news and warner.
Exclusive devotion to Allah is stated as the straight path.
Those who follow Allah's guidance are guarded from going astray and wretchedness.
Allah's creating and guiding are placed together as a source pattern for guidance.
Every messenger receives the same exclusive-divinity revelation and call to worship Allah.
The sending of the messenger is explicitly oriented to all worlds.
Believers recognize truth from the Lord and Allah guides them to a straight path.
Allah gives life and death and orders the night-day succession.
The Criterion is sent down so its bearer may warn all worlds.
Heaven-earth ownership, creation, and the absence of a partner reinforce the sovereignty clause.
Rival objects are unable to control death, life, or resurrection, sharpening the exclusive life-death claim.
A shared declaration of one God and submission retains parallel monotheistic witness without erasing difference.
Allah's creating, providing, causing death, and giving life directly deny any partner in these acts.
Identifies Muhammad as Allah's messenger and the prophet seal, adding an explicit identity boundary.
The prophet is sent as witness, bearer of good news, warner, caller to Allah, and illuminating lamp.
Directly states that the messenger is sent to all people as bearer of good news and warner.
No community lacks a warner, giving a distributed pattern for public messenger warning.
Directly identifies the addressee as among the messengers.
Places that messenger on a straight path.
The revelation's warning reaches whoever is living and establishes the contrary case against deniers.
The book comes down with truth for people, while guided response and error are distinguished.
Combines exclusive divinity with Allah as the living one and Lord of all worlds.
The messenger receives revelation that the God is one and commands direct upright orientation to Him.
Revelation is given to the messenger as a spirit and makes the book and faith known.
That revelation guides to Allah's straight path, whose is all in heaven and earth.
The messenger is commanded to hold fast to what is revealed because he is on a straight path.
A divinely appointed path is to be followed rather than the desires of those without knowledge.
The prior book of Moses is characterized as a guide and mercy before this Arabic confirming book.
Directly orders obedience to Allah and the messenger and warns against voiding deeds.
Repeats the sending of the messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, reinforcing 9:33.
Directly attributes life and death to Allah and makes the final return to Him.
Messengers come with clear proofs, books, and balance, clarifying a public evidentiary mission.
Faith in Allah and His messenger is joined to receiving mercy and a light for walking.
Exclusive divinity and Allah's sovereign names reinforce the no-partner clause.
Repeats the guidance-and-true-religion mission of the messenger, now in a distinct immediate context.
An unlettered messenger recites signs, purifies, and teaches book and wisdom among the unlettered.
Extends that unlettered-messenger setting to others not yet joined to them.
Orders obedience to Allah and the messenger while defining the messenger's burden as clear conveyance.
Allah creates death and life as a trial, reinforcing the paired acts in the focus.
The messenger's task is limited to conveyance from Allah and His messages.
The Qur'an is characterized as a reminder for all worlds.
A messenger from Allah recites purified pages, supplying a compact recitation-and-messenger parallel.
